To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 3D hierarchical nitrogen-doped porous carbon materials (3D-HNCs) were prepared by carbonizing pig lung and applied for the simultaneous determination of catechol, hydroquinone and resorcinol.
a novel 3D hierarchical porous carbon material was prepared from pig lung and applied as electrode for simultaneous determination of catechol, hydroquinone, and resorcinol.

a new electrochemical sensor was successfully constructed by using the HPCs as the electro-active materials, which exhibited high sensitivity, selectivity and stability for dihydroxy-benzene isomers detection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of biomass-based HPCs, and the application of HPCs as electrochemical sensor for simultaneous determination of three isomers of dihydroxybenezene.
the synthesis of HPCs from biomass, and the application in simultaneous determination of dihdroxybenzene.
the synthesis of a novel nitrogen-doped hierarchical porous carbon material (HPCs), which is a promising candidate for the construction of electrochemical sensor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pig lung-derived N-doped HPCs were a promising electrode material for electrochemical sensor.
the HPCs based sensor was a promising method for the simultaneous detection of dihyroxybenzene.

this work provided a novel, low cost and effective strategy for the preparation of N-doped HPCs, which can be used as electrode material to construct electrochemical sensor for detection of dihydrooxybenzene isomer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this work provides a novel and facile strategy to fabricate 3D hierarchical porous carbon from biomass for electrochemical sensor.
the self-template synthesis of biomass precursor was an effective and green strategy to obtain hierarchical porous carbon materials with excellent performance for electrochemical sensor.
the HPCs were successfully applied to the simultaneous detection of dihydric phenols.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HPCs with high graphitic degree and nitrogen-doping could be used as an excellent electrode material for the electrochemical sensor of dihydroxybenezene isomers.
the self-template synthesis of biomass derived HPCs is a promising method to prepare high performance electrochemical sensor.
the pig lung-derived N-doped HPCs are a promising electrode material for the detection of dihydroxylated benzene compounds.
